From my experience, you can only know, from experience.

For example just because a person is nice, doesn't mean they're nice all the time. Maybe they want something.

The best way I found out on how to really know what a person is thinking, is to read their body language. I took a great interest into this, and studied a book or two about it. Then I would go to to a public place, like a bar, and 'people watch'. I could guess what they were talking about just by their movements. I noticed little subtle movements and could pick out the players, the sluts, the smart quiet ones and the shy nymphos.

Knowing body language has made people like me, gotten me raises at work, kept my job, gotten me laid, has made me friends, turned dangerous situations into calm retreats. Knowing is not enough, you must use judgement in every situation.

Here's a book you could read through for free.

https://e-edu.nbu.bg/pluginfile.php/331752/mod_resource/content/0/Allan_and_Barbara_Pease_-_Body_Language_The_Definitive_Book.pdf

It's simple but very effective. I suggest reading it at whatever part interests you most. Don't need to read from start to finish. Read some cues on what a person is showing, then hear them speak and see if it matches their posture. Then you know if they're being honest or not, or they might not be sure at all.

**Daily Devotional**

**March 20**

*6 Being confident of this very thing, that he which hath begun a good work in you will perform it until the day of Jesus Christ: (Philippians 1:6 KJV)*

This is spoken to Christians who are givers to the Kingdom of God, and not just takers. It does not hold true that Jesus will perform His good work in all Christians until the day of the Lord, but is spoken by Paul to mature Christian partners of his. Paul was confident that these believers would continue in the faith until the coming of Jesus again. It is true that some fall away from their trust in Jesus as Savior and become a reprobate (Romans 1:28). Others can lose their salvation by blasphemy against the Holy Ghost (Matthew 12:31-32), or by disobeying Jesus (Hebrews 5:9).

The day of Jesus Christ of course is the second coming of Jesus, and is the time that the church (all Christians) will rise to meet Jesus in the air (Revelation 14:16), and we will all be changed and given new glorified bodies, and be like our Jesus (Philippians 3:21). Take time to think on and contemplate the wonderful things the Lord has planned for us, and has already given us the down payment of the Holy Spirit as earnest for all our future benefits (2 Corinthians 5:5). What a wonderful and gracious God we have to give us so much when we were not worthy of anything. Thank God we were created for His pleasure (Revelation 4:11). Praise God for His love!
